hot-desk.definition: A shared desk used by different people at different times instead of being assigned to one person.
hot-desk.exampleUsage: Members can use any available hot desk.

dedicated-desk.definition: A desk reserved for the regular use of one member in a shared workspace.
dedicated-desk.exampleUsage: His dedicated desk is near the window.

private-office.definition: A workspace intended for one person, usually enclosed by a closable door that helps protect private conversations and information.

phone-booth.definition: A small enclosed shelter designed for making telephone calls.

meeting-room.definition: A room reserved for group meetings, often located in an office, school, hotel, or community center.

lounge-area.definition: An area in a building set aside for sitting and relaxing.

rooftop-terrace.definition: An outdoor area on the roof of a building where people can sit or gather.
rooftop-terrace.exampleUsage: Members ate lunch on the rooftop terrace.

event-space.definition: An area designed to host talks, workshops, meetings, or social events.
event-space.exampleUsage: The company booked the event space for a workshop.

podcast-room.definition: A sound-controlled room equipped for recording spoken audio or podcasts.
podcast-room.exampleUsage: She recorded the interview in the podcast room.

high-speed-wifi.definition: A fast wireless internet connection available within a building or area.
high-speed-wifi.exampleUsage: The coworking space provides high-speed WiFi.

printer.exampleUsage: The printer was used during the activity.
printer.definition: A machine that puts text or images from a computer onto paper.

scanner.definition: A device that turns a paper image or document into a digital file.
scanner.exampleUsage: The scanner was used during the activity.

coffee-machine.definition: A machine that prepares coffee, often automatically from water and coffee beans or capsules.
coffee-machine.exampleUsage: The coffee machine is beside the shared kitchen.

snack-bar.definition: A small business or counter that sells simple meals, snacks, and drinks for customers to eat there or take away.

bike-storage.definition: A secure area where bicycles can be left while their owners are in the building.
bike-storage.exampleUsage: The building has indoor bike storage for members.

shower.definition: A place or device that sprays water over you so you can wash your body.
shower.exampleUsage: The shower was used during the activity.

locker.definition: A small locked compartment for a student’s belongings.

mail-service.definition: A service that receives, stores, or forwards letters and parcels for customers or members.
mail-service.exampleUsage: The virtual office package includes a mail service.

reception.definition: (American football) the act of catching a pass in football.

day-pass.definition: A ticket or permission that allows access to a place or service for one day.
day-pass.exampleUsage: A visitor bought a day pass to use the workspace.

monthly-plan.definition: A service arrangement paid for each month that provides agreed access or benefits.
monthly-plan.exampleUsage: The monthly plan includes workspace access on weekdays.

annual-plan.definition: A detailed year-long guide sets an organization’s, department’s, course’s, or individual’s goals and activities. It also schedules the work and assigns the money, people, and materials needed to complete it during a calendar or fiscal year.

flex-plan.definition: A membership plan that allows flexible use of workspace facilities rather than a permanently assigned place.
flex-plan.exampleUsage: The flex plan suits people who visit only a few days each month.

team-plan.definition: A membership arrangement designed to give a group of coworkers shared access and services.
team-plan.exampleUsage: The startup chose a team plan for six employees.

virtual-office.definition: A service that gives a business an address and office support without requiring a permanent physical office.
virtual-office.exampleUsage: The consultant uses a virtual office for business mail.

meeting-room-credits.definition: A set amount of prepaid or included time that can be used to reserve meeting rooms.
meeting-room-credits.exampleUsage: Her membership includes four meeting-room credits each month.

guest-pass.definition: Temporary permission that allows a member's visitor to enter or use a facility.
guest-pass.exampleUsage: Reception issued a guest pass for the visitor.

community-access.definition: Permission to join shared member areas, events, or communication channels in a community.
community-access.exampleUsage: The plan includes community access and member events.

24-7-access.definition: Permission or ability to enter a place or make use of a service.

networking-event.definition: An organized gathering where people meet to make professional contacts and exchange ideas.
networking-event.exampleUsage: The workspace hosted a networking event for local founders.

workshop.definition: Small workplace where handcrafts or manufacturing are done.

lunch-learn.definition: An informal educational session held around lunchtime, usually combining a short talk with a meal break.
lunch-learn.exampleUsage: The team attended a lunch-and-learn about cybersecurity.

happy-hour.definition: A period when a bar offers alcoholic drinks for less than usual.

pitch-night.definition: An event where people briefly present business or project ideas to an audience.
pitch-night.exampleUsage: Several student teams presented ideas at pitch night.

demo-day.definition: An event where teams demonstrate products, projects, or prototypes to an audience.
demo-day.exampleUsage: The startup showed its prototype at demo day.

mentorship.definition: A lasting, organized relationship in which a more experienced person helps someone less experienced learn, grow, and become part of a social or professional group.

slack-channel.definition: A named conversation space within the Slack messaging service for a particular topic or group.
slack-channel.exampleUsage: Members use the Slack channel for community announcements.

community-manager.definition: A person who supports members, organizes activities, and helps build relationships within a community.
community-manager.exampleUsage: The community manager welcomed new members.

member-directory.definition: A list or searchable record containing information about the members of an organization or community.
member-directory.exampleUsage: The member directory helps coworkers find people with similar skills.
